subject: New Observability Partner: LogixStream - Dataflow & DPA follow-up
messages:
From: Avery Collins <avery.collins@logixstream.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LogixStream onboarding: subprocessor notice and evidence pack

Hi Hannah —

Following our pilot agreement kickoff, I wanted to notify Redwood of a change in LogixStream’s processing architecture that affects telemetry routing for EU customers. We plan to route aggregated observability traces to our new processing cluster in Frankfurt (operated by LogixStream Europe GmbH), while retaining a failover stream to our APAC analytics endpoint.

What’s changing:
- New processing entity: LogixStream Europe GmbH (jurisdiction: DE)
- Purpose: ephemeral observability enrichment, retention window 14 days (raw traces), 90 days (aggregates)
- Data types: application traces, service metrics, anonymized request ids; we do NOT intend to ingest full request payloads.

We’ve attached a subprocessor matrix, a quick dataflow PNG, and a SOC 2 excerpt for the Frankfurt cluster. We propose a short DPA amendment (attached) that adds LogixStream Europe GmbH as a subprocessor.

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Redwood needs any additional evidence for EU residency or controls (I can pull more KMS/partitioning docs).
2) Let us know if the proposed DPA amendment needs changes before DocuSign.
3) If you need a technical contact for a short walkthrough (30m), I can set up time this week.

Apologies for the short notice — we’re aiming for a phased rollout next Tuesday (2 June) but will hold if Redwood requires more review.

Thanks,
Avery Collins
Head of Integrations, LogixStream
attachments: logixstream_subprocessor_matrix_v1.xlsx; logix_dataflow_eu_apac.png; logix_soc2_report_excerpt.pdf; dpa_amendment_proposal.docx

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Avery Collins <avery.collins@logixstream.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LogixStream onboarding: subprocessor notice and evidence pack

Avery —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the attachments. Quick questions so we can triage internally:

1) Residency and egress: can you confirm that raw traces for EU customers remain within the Frankfurt cluster and are not replicated to APAC except for aggregated metrics? The PNG suggests a failover stream; we need a short note on conditions that trigger replication.
2) PII/identifiers: you say "anonymized request ids" — please clarify whether those IDs are reversible or are salted hashes. Any chance that request ids could be linked back to PII in downstream tooling?
3) Access controls & key management: who manages KMS keys for the Frankfurt cluster? Is key material separated by tenant or shared?
4) Evidence: SOC 2 excerpt is helpful — please also provide either an ISO27001 cert (if available) or a recent penetration-test summary for the EU environment.

Operational asks from our side:
- If you plan to add LogixStream Europe GmbH as a subprocessor we will need a short DPA amendment and an internal procurement review (legal + security).
- Please flag whether any subprocessing will be performed by third parties (e.g., cloud provider subcontracts).

Can you send a one-page technical appendix answering the four bullets above and confirm whether you can pause the rollout for Redwood until we finish our review? If you can’t pause, state the earliest rollback window.

I’ll loop in procurement after I have the appendix.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Security & Compliance (Redwood Inference)

From: Avery Collins <avery.collins@logixstream.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, LogixStream Legal <legal@logixstream.io>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LogixStream onboarding: subprocessor notice and evidence pack

Hannah —

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. Answers below and I’ve attached a short appendix (see Drive link in our email and attached files).

1) Residency & egress: raw traces for EU tenants are processed and stored only in our Frankfurt cluster by default. The APAC replication path is strictly a failover and is only used if Frankfurt is unreachable for more than 15 minutes for an active rolling backfill; we can provide the failover runbook. No automatic replication of raw traces to APAC for EU-tagged accounts. Aggregated metrics (non-reversible counters and histograms) are replicated for global product analytics.

2) Identifiers: request ids are salted SHA-256 hashes keyed per-tenant. They are not reversible by LogixStream. We do not maintain mapping tables linking hashes to raw PII. We will add language to the DPA amendment to state this explicitly.

3) KMS & key separation: Frankfurt keys are managed by our cloud provider’s KMS, with tenant-level key wrapping. LogixStream holds no plaintext master key material; customer tenant keys are wrapped with a cluster master key stored in the provider KMS (we will provide a KMS access control matrix).

4) Additional evidence: attached is a redacted penetration test executive summary and the requested SOC 2 Type II excerpt. ISO27001 not held for the EU entity today; we can provide tighter compensating controls in the appendix.

Third parties: the Frankfurt cluster runs on ACME Public Cloud — subcontracts with ACME are noted in the subprocessor matrix. No further downstream subprocessors are scheduled beyond the cloud provider for the initial rollout.

Rollout & pause: we can pause Redwood’s onboarding until sign-off. If you prefer us to proceed, our earliest rollback window is 72 hours from rollout; we will hold changes for your confirmation.

Attached: logixstream_subprocessor_matrix_v1.xlsx; logix_dataflow_eu_apac.png; logix_soc2_report_excerpt.pdf; dpa_amendment_proposal.docx

Let me know if you’d like a quick walkthrough this afternoon.

Best,
Avery

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Collins <avery.collins@logixstream.io>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LogixStream onboarding: subprocessor notice and evidence pack

Avery — thanks for the quick follow-up and the appendix. Per internal procurement and legal review, next items before we can sign the DPA amendment:

- Please insert the explicit non-reversibility language for tenant hashes into the DPA amendment (we’ll share a single-sentence suggestion).
- Provide the KMS access control matrix and the ACME cloud subcontract detail (contact and contract id) as a short PDF.
- Add the Frankfurt failover runbook excerpt (1–2 pages) describing conditions that trigger APAC replication.

If you can make those three updates we’ll prepare the DPA for signature and route to our legal for final redlines. We’d prefer DocuSign for the amendment (link in our related_links).

Can you confirm turnaround on these artifacts? If you can get them to us by EOD Wednesday (27 May), procurement will aim to issue the DocuSign packet Thursday. Otherwise we’ll push to the following week.

Thanks — Hannah will handle the controls acceptance, Kimberly will validate the ACME subcontracting detail.

Marissa Cole
Head of Procurement, Redwood Inference
